title: FATF grey-lists Lebanon
why: Raises compliance friction for Lebanese banks, founders and correspondent payments; still listed at June 2026 plenary.

title: Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire brokered
why: Ended the 2023-24 war; Israel kept the right to strike, setting the pattern of near-daily violations and stalled recovery.

title: Assad regime falls
why: Ends the Hezbollah land bridge and Assad-era smuggling economy; opens a new Syria-Lebanon state-to-state relationship.

title: Aoun and Salam take office
why: New government opens the door to Gulf, US and IMF re-engagement after years of paralysis.

title: Border clashes; Saudi-hosted demarcation deal signed
why: Defence ministers agreed border demarcation and security coordination after deadly Hermel/Qusayr clashes; smuggling crackdown began.

title: Saudi agrees to review Lebanese import ban
why: First formal signal that the 2021 export ban could end, worth about $100m a year to Lebanese exporters.

title: Coastal massacres of Alawites
why: Roughly 1,400 dead; deepened minority fears, sent Alawite refugees into north Lebanon and clouded Western re-engagement.

title: EU lifts most economic sanctions on Syria
why: Reopens Syria to European trade and banking; Lebanese firms can now serve as intermediaries without EU sanctions risk.

title: EU adds Lebanon to high-risk AML list
why: In force 5 Aug 2025; forces enhanced due diligence on EU flows to Lebanon, hitting founders' bank accounts and transfers.

title: UNHCR-IOM organised returns from Lebanon begin
why: Start of the multi-phase plan; Syrian labour supply in Lebanon begins to shrink.

title: Suwayda violence involving Druze, Bedouin, government forces
why: Shows limits of Damascus control; Israel struck Syria, feeding the security-risk premium for investors.

title: Cabinet backs Hezbollah arms-monopoly decision
why: Shiite ministers walked out; state formally commits to disarmament, the basis for Gulf and US conditionality.

title: Cabinet accepts army five-phase disarmament plan
why: South-to-north roadmap becomes the yardstick for US aid, Israeli withdrawal and Gulf trust.

title: Sharaa visits White House; Caesar Act suspended
why: Legitimises Damascus in Washington and unlocks Gulf and Western capital that competes with Lebanon for reconstruction roles.

title: Lebanon-Cyprus EEZ agreement signed and ratified
why: Ends a two-decade gap; clears offshore exploration on the Cyprus side and adds a maritime-border precedent for Syria talks.

title: Caesar Act repealed via NDAA
why: Removes secondary-sanction risk on dealing with Syria; opens the door for Lebanese banks and firms to do Syria business.

title: UNHCR: about 378,000 Syrians returned from Lebanon
why: Cumulative return since Assad's fall; removes a large informal workforce and consumer base from Lebanon.

title: Visa announces partnership with Central Bank of Syria
why: Syrian payments stack re-opens to global rails, a fintech competitor and partner for Lebanese payment firms.

title: Syria-Jordan gas import deal (about 140 MMcf/d)
why: First step of the Arab Gas Pipeline revival that Lebanon's Deir Ammar plant plans to tap.

title: Israel-Syria security talks planned in Paris
why: US-mediated track; Damascus said it agreed 'almost everything' on paper; stalled when the Iran war began.

title: Qatar announces about $430m aid for Lebanon
why: Up to $400m for the power sector plus army fuel and salaries; Qatar is the most active Gulf funder in Lebanon.

title: Saudi-Syria deals worth about $5.3bn
why: Aviation, telecom, utilities: Saudi capital prefers Syria's open field, competing with Lebanon for Gulf attention.

title: US sanctions Jood SARL gold exchange tied to Al-Qard al-Hassan
why: Targets Hezbollah's gold-to-cash liquidity; raises compliance risk for Lebanon's cash and gold trade.

title: US-Israel strikes kill Khamenei; Iran war begins
why: Triggers the regional war that pulls Hezbollah in, closes Hormuz and hits Gulf economies that employ Lebanese.

title: Iranian drones hit AWS data centres in UAE and Bahrain
why: Undermines the Gulf AI-hub premise; raises risk and cost for AI buildout that competes for talent and capital.

title: Hezbollah fires on Israel; 2026 Lebanon war begins
why: Ends 15 months of ceasefire; 1.2m displaced, thousands killed, GDP forecast turns sharply negative.

title: Parliament postpones elections by two years
why: Vote 76-41 pushes elections to 2028, delaying democratic renewal that Gulf and Western donors wanted before big money.

title: Israeli ground invasion of south Lebanon
why: Occupation of about 570-600 sq km, bridges over the Litani destroyed, southern economy cut off.

title: Lebanon expels Iranian ambassador
why: State breaks with Tehran; cuts diplomatic cover for cash and flights, and improves standing with Gulf and West.

title: Returns from Lebanon accelerate after war restarts
why: UNHCR counts more than 464,000 cross-border movements by 22 June; Syria absorbs flows, Lebanon loses labour and rents. [464,000 by 22 June figure not re-verified; UNHCR: over 200,000 crossed into Syria 2-27 Mar 2026]

title: Syria hands 130 detainees back from Lebanese prisons
why: Partial progress on a key Damascus demand; hundreds remain and the issue still blocks the wider reset.

title: Remittances to Lebanon fall 10-15% expected
why: About $6bn a year, roughly half from GCC; Gulf job losses cut the dollar lifeline for about 85% import dependence.

title: First US-Iran two-week ceasefire
why: Temporary relief; Hormuz stays contested and energy prices stay elevated for import-dependent Lebanon.

title: First direct Lebanon-Israel talks in Washington
why: Opens a state-to-state negotiating track hosted by Rubio; first such format in decades.

title: Beirut flights resume after about 40-day suspension
why: Qatar Airways and others return; airport is the country's only international gateway for diaspora and Gulf traffic.

title: US-brokered 10-day Israel-Lebanon truce
why: Extended repeatedly (23 Apr, 15 May); Israel keeps self-defence strikes and its ground positions.

title: UAE bars citizens from travel to Lebanon
why: Gulf tourists, the summer spending base, disappear; lifted 29 June with registration.

title: Hormuz closure roughly doubles Lebanese generator fuel cost
why: Diesel about $700 to $1,400 per tonne; private generator bills up about 35%, feeding 17.5% inflation forecast.

title: Jordan-Syria-Lebanon gas swap agreed
why: Route to feed Deir Ammar (about 450 MW claimed) but needs pipeline repairs and contracts; no dates yet.

title: First Visa/Mastercard trial payment inside Syria in 15 years
why: Syria's card and POS rollout (PAYMERA) starts; Syrian fintech leapfrogs a Lebanon still boxed in by AML listings.

title: Salam visits Damascus
why: Second visit; sets the 'sovereign equals' framework, prioritising border, detainees and returns before trade.

title: UAE sanctions Hezbollah-linked financial network
why: Gulf jurisdictions align with US designations; Lebanese Shiite-linked commerce and remittances face more scrutiny.

title: Saudi lifts five-year ban on Lebanese imports
why: Reopens a market worth about $100m a year; Saudi citizen travel ban to Lebanon stays.

title: Pakistan-mediated interim US-Iran deal (Islamabad memorandum)
why: Promised Hormuz reopening and an end to Hezbollah-Israel fighting; MoU signed 17 June, then broke down.

title: Framework agreement signed in Washington
why: Phased Israeli withdrawal via pilot zones for army deployment; Hezbollah rejects it; no aid package included.

title: UAE lifts Lebanon travel ban for citizens
why: Partial return of Gulf visitors and spending, with mandatory Twajudi registration.

title: Higher Joint Lebanese-Syrian Commission created
why: Institutional channel to review 40+ Assad-era agreements, security and economic ties; first meeting due within two months of 24 Sep.

title: Trump declares US-Iran ceasefire over
why: Renewed strikes and Hormuz disruption; sustained energy-price risk for Lebanon. Later talks via Qatar continue.

title: Lebanon says Syrian electricity import contract 'almost ready'
why: Would cut dependence on EDL's few hours a day; volume and price not yet fixed.

title: Lebanese economy minister meets Sharaa; business council launched
why: Sharaa: 'the economy is more important than politics'; a Lebanese-Syrian Business Council of 11 firms is formed.

title: Aoun meets Trump at White House
why: First Lebanese presidential visit in 17 years; a Washington investment conference for Lebanon was discussed but not scheduled.

title: First three pilot zones announced; one Israeli withdrawal
why: Only one zone handed to the army; no further zones named as of late September.

title: Syria-Lebanon border coordination talks in Beirut (IOM, EU support)
why: Electronic customs links, anti-smuggling and document checks on the 375 km border.

title: World Bank projects Lebanon GDP -6.4% in 2026
why: War erases the 4.2% growth otherwise expected; inflation seen at 17.5%; frames all donor and IMF talks.

title: Syria-Israel US-mediated talks in Jordan
why: Israeli occupation zones in Syria and strikes continue; no deal; Israeli red line on Turkish presence.

title: Syria-Lebanon agree joint team on Tripoli-Homs rail
why: Tender for Lebanese section at about $860k study stage; no construction funding announced.

title: Saudi-Syria joint bank and transport deals
why: Easier Saudi-Syria money transfers plus aviation, rail, road; Syria gets the Gulf corridor Lebanon wanted.

title: Dabousiyah crossing announced to reopen on 9 September
why: Adds a second commercial crossing to ease Jdeidet Yabous, the only one operating; feeds Tripoli-Syria-Gulf trucking. (corrected from 2026-09: sources announce a 9 September reopening; actual opening not confirmed on a read page)

title: IMF staff visit; staff-level agreement hoped by year end
why: Bank Resolution Law amended; full deal awaits the financial gap law; US ties support to reforms.

title: Macron hosts Lebanon and Jordan leaders on army support
why: Army donor conference likely late 2026 or early 2027 after February date lapsed; post-UNIFIL mission options discussed.

title: First Lebanese-Syrian Investment Forum in Beirut
why: About 400 business people, 16 ministers, 20+ opportunities; Chamber of Commerce MoU signed; Damascus edition planned.

title: Salam meets Sharaa at UNGA
why: Agree to work on electricity, rail and energy links; prisoners and border demarcation remain unresolved.

title: Rubio hosts Salam; talks deadlocked on sequencing
why: Israel wants disarmament before withdrawal; Lebanon the reverse; next round slipped to 20 October.

title: Syria faces $1bn half-year deficit; may delay projects
why: Syrian investment pipeline less certain than headlines; tempers the pull on Lebanese capital and talent.

title: Projectile hits vessel in Hormuz; US-Iran talks via Qatar
why: Trump rejected Iran's one-week ceasefire idea on 26 Sep; energy-price risk persists for Lebanon.

title: Iraq fuel-for-services deal: last confirmed renewal March 2025
why: No 2026 renewal found in searches; status of Iraqi heavy fuel supply to EDL is unverified.

title: Erdogan: Turkey's security begins in Aleppo, Damascus, Beirut
why: Ankara positions as a counterweight to Iran and Israel in Lebanon; Tripoli port, rail and power links discussed.
